ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In a recent online survey of 1,700 adults, it was revealed that only 17% felt the Internet was secure. With what degree of confidence can you say that 17% +/- 2% of adults believe that online security is secure?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Treat this as a one-sample proportion confidence-interval question. The survey gives sample size n = 1700 and observed proportion p-hat = 0.17, so 1 - p-hat = 0.83. The desired margin of error is E = 0.02. The standard error is SE = sqrt(p-hat(1 - p-hat)/n) = sqrt(0.17 * 0.83 / 1700) ≈ 0.0091. The z-value corresponding to this margin is z = E / SE = 0.02 / 0.0091 ≈ 2.20. The confidence level is the central normal probability P(-2.20 < Z < 2.20) = 2Φ(2.20) - 1 ≈ 2(0.9861) - 1 = 0.9722, which is about 97.2%.

method.method_draft: Use the survey statement as a one-sample proportion confidence-interval problem. Read from the text that the sample size is n=1700, the observed proportion is p̂=0.17, and the desired margin of error is E=0.02. Compute the standard error for a sample proportion: SE=sqrt(p̂(1-p̂)/n)=sqrt(0.17*0.83/1700)≈0.0091. Find the critical z-value implied by the margin: z=E/SE=0.02/0.0091≈2.20. Convert this z-value to a two-sided central normal probability: confidence = P(-2.20<Z<2.20)=2Φ(2.20)-1≈2(0.9861)-1=0.9722, or about 97.2%.
